regulator: Autorité Ivoirienne de Régulation Pharmaceutique (AIRP) – https://www.airp.ci

facts.title: Regulator and legal basis
facts.body: The AIRP, created by Law 2017-541 of 3 August 2017 (art. 18: no pharmaceutical product may be placed on the market without a marketing authorisation, the AMM) and organised by decree 2018-926, grants AMMs for medicines. Côte d'Ivoire applies the UEMOA regulation 04/2020/CM/UEMOA on homologation, so the dossier, the review clock and the five-year validity are the UEMOA ones. The AIRP publishes no searchable register of authorised medicines yet.

facts.title: UEMOA CTD, in French
facts.body: The dossier follows the UEMOA Common Technical Document (modules 1 to 5) and is filed in French; English submissions with translated annexes draw more questions and longer cycles. Modules 2 to 5 prepared for Senegal or another UEMOA state are reused; module 1 is specific to Côte d'Ivoire.

facts.title: 120 days of regulatory time under UEMOA; 12 to 24 months in practice
facts.body: The UEMOA regulation sets 120 days of regulatory time for a new AMM, a variation or a renewal, 360 days at most, with the clock stopped while the applicant answers. Service providers report 12 to 24 months from a clean CTD submission to the AMM in Côte d'Ivoire; the AIRP publishes no performance figures.

facts.title: Fees set by AIRP decision 007/AIRP/CR of 24 April 2023
facts.body: AMM fees are fixed by a decision of the AIRP's board (Décision 007/AIRP/CR of 24 April 2023, published 12 May 2023). The schedule is not published online; the AIRP gives it on request and each filing carries the receipt of payment. Budget for a fee in the same range as the other UEMOA states (about 1 to 2 million FCFA per product) until confirmed.

facts.title: Abridged dossier for WHO-prequalified products
facts.body: Under the UEMOA annexes a WHO-prequalified product files an abridged dossier through the collaborative procedure: the authority obtains WHO's assessment report and asks for modules 4 and 5 only when needed.

facts.title: Import authorisation per shipment
facts.body: Each import of pharmaceutical products needs an AIRP import authorisation, filed at the AIRP mail office with the complete dossier and the fee receipt; it is valid three months, renewable once, for a single import. Medicines sit in category 0 of the UEMOA common external tariff (no customs duty, community levies apply) and are exempt from VAT.

facts.title: Essential list 2024, public procurement through the Nouvelle PSP
facts.body: The national essential medicines and biomedical equipment list (LNME 2024) is set by order 00848 MSHPCMU/CAB of 10 September 2024, with facility levels A to E and the WHO AWaRe class for antibiotics. The Nouvelle Pharmacie de la Santé Publique (NPSP-CI) buys for the public sector and aims to source 20% locally by 2026 and 40% by 2028. Pharmacy prices are regulated.

facts.title: Five-year validity, suspensions published
facts.body: An AMM is valid five years (UEMOA regulation 04/2020). The AIRP publishes suspensions and withdrawals of AMMs and runs market surveillance campaigns on quality.

routes.label: Full review (UEMOA national procedure)
routes.description: Default route: UEMOA CTD in French filed with the AIRP, screening, expert evaluation, national commission, AMM. 120 days of regulatory time under the regulation; 12 to 24 months reported in practice. Fee per AIRP decision 007/2023, given on request.

routes.label: WHO prequalification (abridged dossier)
routes.description: A WHO-prequalified product files an abridged dossier under the collaborative procedure; the AIRP relies on WHO's assessment report.
